entries.head: fall out

senses.en: to argue with someone and stop being friendly

example.en: The two of them fell out over money and stopped talking.
example.zh: 他俩为了钱闹翻，后来就不说话了。

entries.l1_note: 闹翻是 fall out (with)；fall out 也指掉头发、掉牙。

entries.head: let down

senses.en: to make someone disappointed by not doing what they expected

example.en: I promised to help and then let her down at the last minute.
example.zh: 我答应了帮忙，结果最后一刻让她失望了。

entries.l1_note: “让我失望”不是 make me disappointed 才自然；let me down 更口语。

entries.head: stand up

senses.en: to fail to meet someone you had a date with

example.en: She waited an hour at the restaurant — he stood her up.
example.zh: 她在餐厅等了一小时，他放了她鸽子。

entries.l1_note: 放某人鸽子是 stand someone up，代词夹中间；blow off 接的是事/安排（blow off a meeting）。不说 stand up someone。

entries.head: give in

senses.zh: 被说服或顶不住而妥协
senses.en: to stop resisting and accept what someone wants

example.en: I gave in and ordered fries at midnight.
example.zh: 我最后还是妥协了，半夜点了薯条。

entries.l1_note: give in 是让步，give up 是放弃；中文都叫“算了”，英语不一样。

entries.head: make up for

senses.en: to do something good to replace something bad

example.en: I missed her birthday, so I'm making up for it this weekend.
example.zh: 我错过了她生日，这周末补上。

entries.l1_note: “弥补”不是 make up it（顺序错）；make up for 后面跟弥补的事，代词不能插进短语。

entries.head: sort out

senses.en: to solve a problem or disagreement

example.en: We need to sort this out before it gets worse.
example.zh: 得在变糟之前把这事解决掉。

entries.l1_note: 解决矛盾是 sort out，不是 solve out（中式）。

entries.head: hash out

senses.en: to discuss something until you agree

example.en: Let's hash out the details before the meeting.
example.zh: 开会前先把细节谈拢。

entries.l1_note: hash out 是美式口语，指谈出结果，不是随便聊聊。

entries.head: patch up

senses.en: to repair a relationship after a fight

example.en: They patched things up after a week of silence.
example.zh: 冷战一周后他们和好了。

entries.l1_note: 修补关系是 patch up；make up 更口语、更常见。

entries.head: shut out

example.en: She's been shutting me out since the argument.
example.zh: 吵架之后她一直把我排除在外。

entries.l1_note: 冷落是 shut out，不是 close the door to（太字面）。

entries.head: freeze out

senses.en: to make someone feel unwelcome until they leave

example.en: The new manager froze out anyone who disagreed with him.
example.zh: 新经理把不同意他的人都排挤走了。

entries.l1_note: 排挤是 freeze out，比 ignore 更有“逼走”的意思。

entries.head: storm off

example.en: He stormed off in the middle of dinner.
example.zh: 他饭吃到一半就甩脸走了。

entries.l1_note: 愤然离开是 storm off，不是 leave angrily（太直白）。

entries.head: walk out
entries.zh: 为抗议离开；罢工；离开家庭

senses.en: to leave a place as a protest

example.en: Half the team walked out of the meeting.
example.zh: 一半人从会上退场了。

senses.en: to stop working as a protest

example.en: The factory workers walked out over unpaid overtime.
example.zh: 工厂工人因为加班费没发罢工了。

senses.en: to leave your family and not return

example.en: He walked out on his family after the argument.
example.zh: 吵架之后他离开了家。

entries.l1_note: walk out 是抗议性离开；walk out on sb 是抛下某人。

entries.head: back down

example.en: Neither side was willing to back down.
example.zh: 两边都不肯让步。

entries.l1_note: back down 是在争执中退让；back off 是“离远点、别逼我”。

entries.head: back off

senses.en: to stop pushing someone or something

example.en: Back off — I said I'd think about it.
example.zh: 别逼了，我说了会考虑。

entries.l1_note: back off 语气硬，常用于让人别再追问。

entries.head: hold out

senses.en: to refuse to agree or give in

example.en: They held out for a better offer.
example.zh: 他们一直撑着等更好的条件。

entries.l1_note: hold out 是坚持；hold out for 是坚持等更好的。

entries.head: stand up for

example.en: She stood up for me when everyone else stayed quiet.
example.zh: 别人都不吭声的时候她替我说话。

entries.l1_note: 维护是 stand up for；stand up to 是敢于面对强者。

entries.head: stick up for

senses.en: to defend someone, especially a friend

example.en: Stick up for your brother instead of laughing.
example.zh: 别笑了，替你说句话去。

entries.l1_note: stick up for 是美式口语，和 stand up for 同义。

entries.head: speak up

senses.en: to say what you think openly

example.en: If something feels wrong, speak up in the meeting.
example.zh: 觉得不对就在会上说出来。

entries.l1_note: speak up 有两个意思：说大声点、敢于发声。

entries.head: fire back

senses.en: to reply angrily or quickly to criticism

example.en: She fired back before he could finish the sentence.
example.zh: 他话没说完她就回击了。

entries.l1_note: 回击是 fire back；开火也是 fire，但这里指嘴上。

entries.head: lash out

senses.en: to suddenly attack someone in anger

example.en: He lashed out at me for something that wasn't my fault.
example.zh: 他为了不是我的错的事冲我发火。

entries.l1_note: lash out 是突然攻击，常跟 at；不是“甩出去”。

entries.head: snap at

senses.en: to speak angrily and briefly to someone

example.en: Sorry I snapped at you — I didn't sleep.
example.zh: 抱歉冲你发火了，我没睡好。

entries.l1_note: snap at 是语气凶，不是咬人（狗才 bite）。

entries.head: tear into

example.en: The boss tore into the whole team after the launch failed.
example.zh: 上线失败后老板把整个组骂了一顿。

entries.l1_note: tear into 是猛烈批评；tear up 是撕碎，别混。

entries.head: have it out

senses.en: to discuss a disagreement openly until it is settled

example.en: We finally had it out and cleared the air.
example.zh: 我们终于摊牌，把话说开了。

entries.l1_note: 摊牌是 have it out (with sb)，不是 have a fight。

entries.head: let off

example.en: He got let off with a warning.
example.zh: 他挨了个警告就被放了。

entries.l1_note: 放过是 let off；let out 是放出来、放宽衣服。
collocations: let someone off with a warning

entries.head: cut off

senses.en: to stop someone having contact or support

example.en: He cut off contact with his old friends after the move.
example.zh: 搬走之后他和老朋友都断了联系。

entries.l1_note: 断绝联系是 cut off contact；cut off 也指电话断线。

entries.head: brush off

senses.en: to ignore someone's complaint or idea

example.en: She brushed off my concerns like they didn't matter.
example.zh: 她把我的担心当耳旁风。

entries.l1_note: 敷衍是 brush off，不是 brush（刷）。

entries.head: push around

senses.en: to treat someone badly and order them about

example.en: Don't let the senior staff push you around.
example.zh: 别让老员工呼来喝去。

entries.l1_note: 欺负是 push around，不是 bully around（无此说法）。

entries.head: pick on

senses.en: to keep treating one person unfairly

example.en: Why do you always pick on him?
example.zh: 你为什么总针对他？

entries.l1_note: 针对是 pick on，不是 pick（挑东西）。

entries.head: gang up on

senses.en: when several people unite against one person

example.en: They ganged up on me in the group chat.
example.zh: 他们在群里合伙对付我。

entries.l1_note: 合伙对付是 gang up on，不是 together against（中式）。

entries.head: side with

senses.en: to support one person in an argument

example.en: My mom always sides with my sister.
example.zh: 我妈永远站我姐那边。

entries.l1_note: 站队是 side with，不是 stand with（那是并肩站）。

entries.head: get away with
entries.zh: 侥幸逃过；做了坏事没被发现

senses.en: to not be punished for something

example.en: He copied the report and got away with it.
example.zh: 他抄了报告，居然没被发现。

entries.l1_note: get away with + 事情；不是“和……一起离开”。

entries.head: go back on

senses.en: to fail to do what you promised

example.en: He went back on his promise to split the rent.
example.zh: 他说好平摊房租，后来又反悔了。

entries.l1_note: go back on a promise/word/deal；介词 on 不能换成 to。

entries.head: tell off

example.en: My manager told me off for missing the deadline.
example.zh: 经理因为我错过截止日期训了我一顿。

entries.l1_note: tell someone off；代词夹中间：tell him off。不是“告诉某人离开”。
collocations: tell someone off for being late

entries.head: stay clear of

example.en: Stay clear of that store — they overcharge tourists.
example.zh: 别去那家店，他们宰游客。

entries.l1_note: stay clear of / steer clear of 都表示“远离”。

entries.head: have it out with

senses.en: to discuss a problem openly and angrily

example.en: I finally had it out with my roommate about the rent.
example.zh: 我终于跟室友把房租的事摊开了。

entries.l1_note: have it out with someone 是把矛盾摊开谈；不是“拿出来”。

entries.head: stand one's ground

senses.en: to not change your opinion under pressure

example.en: She stood her ground in the negotiation.
example.zh: 谈判中她坚持了自己的立场。

entries.l1_note: stand one's ground 是“坚持立场”；hold one's ground 同义。

entries.head: get into trouble

senses.en: to get into a difficult situation

example.en: He got into trouble for sharing the client's data.
example.zh: 他因为泄露客户数据惹了麻烦。

entries.l1_note: get into trouble 是惹麻烦；get someone into trouble 是让某人惹麻烦。

entries.head: give someone a hard time

senses.en: to criticize or make things difficult for someone

example.en: The interviewer gave me a hard time about my gap year.
example.zh: 面试官一直追问我空档期的事。

entries.l1_note: give someone a hard time 是“为难/刁难”；不是“给某人一段艰难时光”。

entries.head: catch someone off guard

senses.en: to surprise someone who is not ready

example.en: The sudden question caught me off guard.
example.zh: 那个突然的问题让我措手不及。

entries.l1_note: catch someone off guard 是“让某人措手不及”；不是“抓住警卫”。

entries.head: at someone's expense

example.en: He made a joke at his coworker's expense.
example.zh: 他拿同事开涮。

entries.l1_note: at someone's expense 是“以某人为代价/拿某人开涮”。

entries.head: close in on

example.en: The deadline is closing in on us.
example.zh: 截止日期越来越近了。

entries.l1_note: close in on + 目标；不是“关在里面”。

entries.head: egg on

example.en: His friends egged him on to argue with the manager.
example.zh: 他朋友怂恿他去跟经理吵。

entries.l1_note: egg someone on 是怂恿；不是“下蛋”。

entries.head: be faced with

example.en: We're faced with a much tighter deadline.
example.zh: 我们面临更紧的截止日期。

entries.l1_note: be faced with + 问题；face 单独用是面对。

entries.head: force into

example.en: Don't force him into a decision he's not ready for.
example.zh: 别逼他做一个还没准备好的决定。

entries.l1_note: force someone into + 名词/doing；不是“用力”。

entries.head: interfere with

example.en: Don't let side projects interfere with your main work.
example.zh: 别让副业影响主业。

entries.l1_note: interfere with + 事情；interfere in 是插手。

entries.head: lay into

example.en: The coach laid into the team after the loss.
example.zh: 输球后教练把队员痛骂了一顿。

entries.l1_note: lay into someone 是痛骂/攻击；不是“躺进去”。

entries.head: quarrel with

example.en: He quarreled with his roommate about the bills.
example.zh: 他因为账单跟室友吵了一架。

entries.l1_note: quarrel with someone about something；不是“争论”。

entries.head: reduce to

example.en: The argument reduced to a fight over money.
example.zh: 争吵最后变成了为钱打架。

entries.l1_note: reduce to 可指“简化为/使沦为”；不是“减少”。

entries.head: throw at

example.en: They threw the question at me in the meeting.
example.zh: 会上他们突然把问题抛给我。

entries.l1_note: throw something at someone；不是“扔给”。

entries.head: yield to

example.en: He finally yielded to the pressure.
example.zh: 他最终向压力让步了。

entries.l1_note: yield to + 压力/诱惑；不是“生产”。

entries.head: back away

example.en: He backed away when the argument got loud.
example.zh: 争吵升级时他退缩了。

entries.l1_note: back away 是不及物；back away from + 人/事。

entries.head: butt out

example.en: Butt out — this is between me and my roommate.
example.zh: 别插手，这是我和室友之间的事。

entries.l1_note: butt out 是别多管闲事；不礼貌。

entries.head: drop back

example.en: The crowd dropped back to let the ambulance through.
example.zh: 人群往后退，让救护车过去。

entries.l1_note: drop back 是不及物“后退”；不是“掉在后面”。

entries.head: face off

example.en: The two managers faced off in the meeting.
example.zh: 两个经理在会上对峙。

entries.l1_note: face off 是不及物“对峙”；不是“脸掉了”。

entries.head: gang up

example.en: They ganged up on the new employee.
example.zh: 他们联手对付新员工。

entries.l1_note: gang up on someone 是联手对付；不是“成群”。

entries.head: have it in for

example.en: The coach has had it in for him since day one.
example.zh: 教练从第一天就跟他过不去。

entries.l1_note: have it in for someone 是“跟某人过不去”；不是“有它”。

entries.head: jerk around

example.en: Stop jerking me around and give me a straight answer.
example.zh: 别耍我了，给我个准话。

entries.l1_note: jerk someone around 是耍人；不礼貌。

entries.head: keep back

example.en: She kept back her anger during the call.
example.zh: 打电话时她忍住了怒火。

entries.l1_note: keep back + 情绪/人；不是“保持后面”。

entries.head: look down on

example.en: Don't look down on people who work with their hands.
example.zh: 别看不起靠双手吃饭的人。

entries.l1_note: look down on + 人；不是“往下看”。

entries.head: mouth off

example.en: He mouthed off to the security guard.
example.zh: 他跟保安乱顶嘴。

entries.l1_note: mouth off 是乱顶嘴/抱怨；不礼貌。

entries.head: pick apart

example.en: The reviewer picked apart every sentence.
example.zh: 评论者逐句挑刺。

entries.l1_note: pick apart + 作品/说法；不是“拆开”。

entries.head: pull back

example.en: The company pulled back from the deal.
example.zh: 公司退出了这笔交易。

entries.l1_note: pull back 是不及物“撤回/后退”；不是“拉回来”。

entries.head: rough up

example.en: The gang roughed him up in the alley.
example.zh: 那帮人在巷子里打了他一顿。

entries.l1_note: rough someone up 是殴打；口语。

entries.head: screw over

example.en: The landlord screwed us over on the deposit.
example.zh: 房东在押金上坑了我们。

entries.l1_note: screw someone over 是坑害；口语。

entries.head: shake down

example.en: The gang shook down local shop owners.
example.zh: 那帮人勒索当地店主。

entries.l1_note: shake down 是勒索/搜查；不是“摇下来”。

entries.head: stab in the back

example.en: He stabbed his partner in the back over the deal.
example.zh: 他为了这笔交易在背后捅了合伙人一刀。

entries.l1_note: stab someone in the back 是背叛；不是“刺背”。

entries.head: stir up

example.en: He stirred up trouble between the two teams.
example.zh: 他在两个团队之间挑事。

entries.l1_note: stir up + 麻烦/情绪；不是“搅拌”。

entries.head: storm out

example.en: She stormed out of the meeting.
example.zh: 她气冲冲地离开了会议室。

entries.l1_note: storm out 是气冲冲离开；不是“风暴出去”。

entries.head: strike back

example.en: The company struck back with a lawsuit.
example.zh: 公司用诉讼反击。

entries.l1_note: strike back 是不及物“反击”；不是“打回去”。

entries.head: talk back

example.en: Don't talk back to your parents like that.
example.zh: 别那样跟父母顶嘴。

entries.l1_note: talk back to + 人；不是“说回去”。

entries.head: talk down

example.en: He talks down to everyone on the team.
example.zh: 他对团队里每个人都居高临下。

entries.l1_note: talk down to someone 是居高临下；talk down 也可指“说服降落”。

entries.head: trick into

example.en: They tricked him into signing the contract.
example.zh: 他们骗他签了合同。

entries.l1_note: trick someone into + 名词/doing；不是“骗进去”。

entries.head: twist someone's arm

example.en: They twisted my arm until I agreed to present.
example.zh: 他们软磨硬泡，直到我答应做演示。

entries.l1_note: twist someone's arm 是“软磨硬泡说服”；不是“拧胳膊”。

entries.head: bite someone's head off

example.en: Don't bite my head off — I just asked a question.
example.zh: 别冲我发火，我只是问了一句。

entries.l1_note: bite someone's head off 是突然发火；不是“咬头”。

example.en: They had a fight about money.
example.zh: 他们为钱吵了一架。

example.en: We argued about where to eat.
example.zh: 我们为去哪吃饭争了起来。

example.en: Don't shout at the kids.
example.zh: 别冲孩子大喊。

example.en: He lost his temper and left the room.
example.zh: 他发了脾气，离开了房间。

example.en: Count to ten before you reply.
example.zh: 回复之前先数到十。

example.en: Let's talk it over when we're both calm.
example.zh: 我们冷静下来好好谈谈。

example.en: Say sorry and mean it.
example.zh: 道歉要真诚。

example.en: It's hard to forgive someone who never apologizes.
example.zh: 从不道歉的人很难原谅。

example.en: This is all wrong; start again.
example.zh: 全错了，重来。

example.en: That was a bad move; now we're late.
example.zh: 那步走错了，现在我们迟了。

example.en: You should have told me earlier.
example.zh: 你本该早点告诉我。

example.en: Who let you do that without asking?
example.zh: 谁允许你不问就做？

example.en: What's the big idea? You can't park here.
example.zh: 你在搞什么？这儿不能停车。

example.en: Being tired is no excuse for being rude.
example.zh: 累了不是没礼貌的借口。

example.en: You never listen when I talk about work.
example.zh: 我聊工作的时候你从来不听。

example.en: Cut it out; I'm trying to work.
example.zh: 别闹了，我在干活。

example.en: Look what you did to the carpet.
example.zh: 看看你把地毯弄成什么样了。

example.en: Complaining now doesn't help.
example.zh: 现在抱怨没用。

example.en: Be careful with the hot water.
example.zh: 小心热水。

example.en: Mind your head; the door is low.
example.zh: 小心碰头，门很低。

entries.head: keep an eye out for something

example.en: Keep an eye out for the delivery.
example.zh: 留意一下快递。

entries.head: do not go near the edge

example.en: Don't go near the edge of the platform.
example.zh: 别靠近站台边缘。

example.en: Look both ways before you cross.
example.zh: 过马路前看两边。

example.en: Heads up — the boss is coming.
example.zh: 注意，老板来了。

entries.head: do not open the door to strangers

example.en: Don't open the door to strangers.
example.zh: 别给陌生人开门。

example.en: Keep away from the fire.
example.zh: 离火远点。

example.en: Finish it today, or else.
example.zh: 今天必须做完，否则看着办。

example.en: You will be sorry if you skip the meeting.
example.zh: 你缺席会议会后悔的。

example.en: You will pay for this.
example.zh: 你会付出代价的。

example.en: Don't push me; I'm already angry.
example.zh: 别逼我，我已经很生气了。

example.en: That joke crossed the line.
example.zh: 那个玩笑越界了。

example.en: This is your last warning.
example.zh: 这是最后一次警告。

example.en: You'll be in trouble if the teacher sees this.
example.zh: 老师看到这个你就有麻烦了。

entries.head: if I catch you doing something

example.en: If I catch you copying again, you'll fail.
example.zh: 再让我抓到你抄，就不及格。

entries.head: don't say I didn't warn you

example.en: Don't say I didn't warn you.
example.zh: 别说我没提醒你。

example.en: Just you wait; he'll come back.
example.zh: 你就等着瞧，他会回来的。

example.en: On the other hand, the rent is cheaper here.
example.zh: 另一方面，这里房租便宜。

example.en: Hold on a second; that's not what I said.
example.zh: 且慢，我不是那个意思。

example.en: That's not the point; we're talking about safety.
example.zh: 这不是重点，我们在说安全。

example.en: Yes, but we don't have the budget.
example.zh: 话虽如此，但我们没预算。

entries.head: I would not go that far

example.en: I would not go that far; it's not that bad.
example.zh: 我不会那么说，没那么糟。

example.en: Talk is cheap; show me the plan.
example.zh: 说空话容易，拿方案出来。

example.en: Not necessarily; it depends on the weather.
example.zh: 未必，要看天气。

example.en: You have it all wrong; I never said that.
example.zh: 你完全搞错了，我没那么说。

example.en: I would not say so; she's actually quite careful.
example.zh: 我倒不这么看，她其实很细心。

example.en: That's not true; I was here all night.
example.zh: 不是真的，我整晚都在这儿。

example.en: Not in a million years would I lend him my car.
example.zh: 我一百万年也不会把车借给他。

example.en: Most parents are against the new rule.
example.zh: 大多数家长反对新规定。

example.en: I have my doubts about this plan.
example.zh: 我对这个计划表示怀疑。

example.en: You want to sell the house? Over my dead body.
example.zh: 你想卖房？休想。

example.en: Not so fast; we haven't agreed yet.
example.zh: 且慢，我们还没同意。

example.en: If you're going to argue, I'm out.
example.zh: 你们要吵，我不参加。

example.en: I object to changing the date again.
example.zh: 我反对再改日期。

example.en: Not on my watch; we follow the rules.
example.zh: 在我这儿不行，我们按规矩来。

example.en: It's okay to say no to extra work.
example.zh: 拒绝额外工作是没问题的。

example.en: Not a chance; I'm not working this weekend.
example.zh: 没门儿，这周末我不加班。
